body:
## What goes wrong

A review's `photoUrls` are client-supplied and never checked for ownership: `ReviewService.createReview` does `review.setPhotoUrls(request.getPhotoUrls())` (line 93), copying the request verbatim. GDPR erasure then **physically deletes every URL in the erased customer's reviews** from storage, under the erasing tenant.

D-09 refuses only a key from *another* tenant. So a customer with a COMPLETED order can post a review whose `photoUrls` are the shop's **own public product or shop image URLs**, then file a DSAR erasure. The vendor's catalogue images, including ref-counted `media_asset` derivatives, get deleted.

## Evidence

- `ReviewService.java:93` copies the list verbatim. `rg -uu` finds no review-photo upload path in the frontend, which only renders `review.photoUrls` (`shop-detail-client.tsx:719`), so the field is set only through the API, with any URL.
- It predates PR #770. On `origin/main`, `GdprService` deletes `review.getPhotoUrls()` (around line 204-208) **before** `reviewRepository.saveAll` (line 221). Because that save failed (issue #764), every erasure attempt already deleted the objects and then rolled back. PR #770 keeps the deletion (moved to after commit) but does not introduce it.
- Found by the round-1 `/code-review` of PR #770. Not reproduced end to end against a live store.

## Fix shape

Validate `photoUrls` when a review is created: only keys the reviewer uploaded, under a review-photo prefix, or registered as review media. Also, or instead, make the erasure delete only objects that no product, shop or `media_asset` row references. Add a test in which a review naming a product image URL is erased and the product image survives.
title: Review photoUrls are unvalidated, so a customer's GDPR erasure can delete the vendor's own product images

body:
## What goes wrong

`scripts/check-doc-citations.sh` fails open when it cannot parse a YAML input. If python3 cannot load `docs/ops/terminal-states.yaml`, the script prints

```
VOID: cannot extract YAML citations from docs/ops/terminal-states.yaml (see message above)
  docs/ops/terminal-states.yaml              citations=0
```

and still ends `PASS: all 28 verified citation(s) across 8 doc(s) …` with **rc=0**. The register's 17 citations silently drop out of the check. The project's own rule says an unparseable input must exit non-zero (VOID = 2), never 0.

## Observed

On 2026-09-30, while preparing PR #768, the first run of `bash scripts/check-doc-citations.sh docs/ops/terminal-states.yaml` happened without a conda env active. The machine's python PATH shim refused bare `python3`, and the result was the VOID line above, `citations=0` and rc=0. With the env active, the same command reported `citations=17` and rc=0. The round-2 verifier of #768 reproduced the fail-open on both trees.

CI is unaffected in practice, because runners have a working python3 with PyYAML. Any local run, or a runner without PyYAML, gets a false green.

## Fix shape

When an input's extractor VOIDs, the whole run must exit 2, as the other gates do on missing tooling. Add a fail-direction arm: a run with python3 unavailable, or given an unparseable YAML fixture, must exit 2.
title: check-doc-citations.sh fails OPEN: a YAML input it cannot parse is reported VOID, counted as 0 citations, and the run still exits 0

body:
## What goes wrong

`GdprService` erasure (Article 17) anonymises a customer's reviews with `reviewRepository.saveAll(reviews)` **after** it has already deleted the review photos from storage. `reviews` has FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY (V35:83) and only two policies: `reviews_tenant_read` (SELECT) and `reviews_tenant_write` (**FOR INSERT** only, V51:95). There is no UPDATE policy, so the anonymising UPDATE matches 0 rows for the application role.

Expected consequence for any customer who has left a review:
- the photos are deleted from Blob storage (not transactional);
- Hibernate rejects the 0-row UPDATE (unexpected row count), so the erasure transaction rolls back;
- the review keeps the customer's name, email and comment, and **no `ErasureRecord` is written**.

A second problem sits in the same loop: `findByCustomerEmail` runs under `reviews_tenant_read`, which shows PUBLISHED reviews across tenants, so the loop can also pick up another tenant's reviews carrying the same email.

## Reproduced (dev DB, one transaction, rolled back)

As `jtoye_app` (rolsuper=f, rolbypassrls=f), with `app.current_tenant_id` pinned to tenant `…0001`:

```
orders_visible=67
INSERT 0 1                 -- review inserted (INSERT policy allows it)
review_visible=1           -- the row IS visible under the pinned tenant
UPDATE 0                   -- the anonymising UPDATE matches nothing
name_after=Repro           -- PII unchanged
ROLLBACK
post_rollback=0            -- no residue
```

Not reproduced end to end: the full erasure call. The Hibernate rejection of a 0-row UPDATE is inferred from standard behaviour, not observed. No integration test inserts a review before erasing, which is why the suites stay green.

## Provenance

This predates Phase 36. `main` has the identical delete-then-`saveAll` order, and no UPDATE policy has existed on `reviews` since V27. Found by PR #763 review round 1 (the PR only changed how deleted photos are counted, WR-02).

## Fix shape (for whoever takes it)

- A tenant-scoped UPDATE policy on `reviews` via `current_tenant_id()` (a new migration, V67).
- Scope the erasure's review lookup to the caller's tenant.
- Delete the photos only after the anonymisation commits (for example `afterCommit`), so a failed erasure destroys nothing.
- A NOSUPERUSER Testcontainers test that erases a customer who has a review with photos.
title: GDPR erasure fails for any customer with a review: reviews has no UPDATE policy, and photos are deleted before the rollback

body:
## What

`/dashboard/media/review` (the vendor Image review page) renders its empty state, **"Nothing needs review"**, when the review-queue request **fails**. The error toast "Couldn't load the review queue — Check your connection and try again." appears on top of it. A vendor who dismisses or misses the toast is told their queue is empty when it was never loaded, and rejected uploads that need a Re-upload stay hidden.

## Observed (2026-09-29, local compose stack)

Signed in as `admin-user` at 1280px, with the browser unable to reach the API. The cause was core-java recreated onto host port 9091 while the bundle calls `http://localhost:9090`; the port-range trap is recorded in #671. The page showed at the same time:

- the empty-state card: "Nothing needs review / Rejected uploads and images flagged for a content check appear here…"
- the toast: "Couldn't load the review queue / Check your connection and try again."
- sidebar: "No shop access" (the same failed-fetch cause)

The database held 3 FAILED `media_asset` rows for that tenant at the time. Once the API was reachable again, the same page correctly listed 3 "Upload rejected" cards with Re-upload buttons.

## Expected

On a failed load, show an error state (with a Retry) in place of the list, never the "Nothing needs review" empty state. The empty state should render only after a SUCCESSFUL load that returned zero items.

## Repro

Make the browser-side API unreachable, for example by stopping core-java or pointing `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` at a closed port, then open `/dashboard/media/review` as a vendor. Last change to the page: Phase 24 (#256). Phase 36 did not touch it.
title: Media review page shows "Nothing needs review" when the review queue failed to load

body:
## What

`scripts/check-doc-citations.sh` reports **PASS, rc=0** when its YAML citation extraction for a doc is **VOID**. Its own header says VOID is exit 2 ("could not evaluate"); here a VOID sub-step is swallowed and the doc is silently counted as having zero citations.

## Observed (2026-09-29, on main's tree at db725c94 + the #760 branch)

On a machine where a bare `python3` is refused (the machine's Python shim), a local run prints:

```
VOID: cannot extract YAML citations from docs/ops/terminal-states.yaml (see message above)
  docs/ops/terminal-states.yaml              citations=0
  violations  0
PASS: all 28 verified citation(s) across 8 doc(s) resolve to lines that support their claim (7 uncheckable).
rc=0
```

## Mechanism

`scripts/check-doc-citations.sh:395`:

```bash
done <<< "$(citations_in "$doc")"
```

`citations_in` calls `void()` (line 60: `echo "VOID: $*" >&2; exit 2`) when the YAML extraction fails. That `exit 2` runs inside the `$( … )` command substitution, so it exits only the subshell. The enclosing loop reads empty input, the doc scores `citations=0`, and the run passes because other docs carried citations. Any failure of the extraction step fails open the same way, for example a runner without PyYAML, and not only this machine's shim.

## Fix shape

Capture the substitution's status before the loop: `out=$(citations_in "$doc"); rc=$?; [ $rc -eq 2 ] && exit 2`, then feed `$out` to the loop. Prove it both ways: make the extraction fail and require exit 2; on a healthy tree require exit 0.

Found by review round 1 of #760 and reproduced there. It predates that PR (the script was last changed in f0ed2763), so it is filed here rather than fixed in it.
title: check-doc-citations.sh passes (rc=0) when a doc's YAML citation extraction is VOID

body:
The daily base-image freshness scan found fixable CRITICAL/HIGH
vulnerabilities in a published image. The `Trivy image gate` in
`.github/workflows/ci-cd.yaml` uses the same flags and the same pinned
action, so **the next push to `main` will fail this leg** — on whatever
commit happens to land, which will have nothing to do with the cause.

### Triage, in order

1. **Rebuild first, before changing anything.** The Dockerfile `FROM`
   lines pin floating tags, so the published image can be carrying a base
   that upstream has already respun. Re-running `build-and-push` on an
   unchanged tree genuinely fixes a large share of these. If it does,
   nothing further is needed.
2. **If a rebuild does not clear it, add the named package to the runner
   stage's remediation line.** This is the lever, and it is already
   exercised in both images that have needed it:
   `core-java/Dockerfile` carries
   `apk upgrade --no-cache libexpat p11-kit p11-kit-trust`, and
   `frontend/Dockerfile` carries
   `apk --no-cache upgrade libcrypto3 libssl3` plus the removal of npm's
   bundled dependency tree from the runner stage. The packages are named
   DELIBERATELY rather than blanket-upgraded; see the comment block in
   `core-java/Dockerfile` for why, and do not replace it with a bare
   `apk upgrade`.
3. **If the finding is not in an apk package** (for example a
   language-level dependency bundled inside the base image), check whether
   the component is used at runtime at all. `frontend/Dockerfile` deletes
   npm from the runner stage for exactly this reason — that removes the
   whole finding class instead of chasing each CVE. Measured 2026-08-03:
   all six of `node:24-alpine`'s findings under the gate's flags live in
   npm's bundled tree, and that one line clears every one of them.
4. **If none of the above can make it pass, STOP and escalate.** A gate
   that no change to this repository can satisfy is a broken gate, not a
   strict one, and the fix is a policy decision — not a quiet `--severity`
   edit or a suppression file added under deadline pressure.

### What NOT to do

Do not widen `severity`, drop `ignore-unfixed`, or move the gate back to
`format: sarif` with an `exit-code` — sarif mode makes Trivy scan ALL
severities, so the gate would then fire on LOW/MEDIUM too. That regression
is guarded by `scripts/check-image-supply-chain.sh`.

Do not close this issue because CI went green on a rerun. The DB moves
daily; green today says nothing about tomorrow. Close it when the image no
longer carries the finding.

**Image:** `ghcr.io/bralabee/jtoye-core-java:latest`

**Scan run:** https://github.com/Bralabee/JToye_OaaS_2026/actions/runs/36532459312

Full Trivy table is in the `Trivy image scan` step of that run.
title: Base-image CVEs block publishing: jtoye-core-java

body:
## What broke, observed

`base-image-freshness.yml`'s **"Open or refresh the tracking issue"** step has had an unterminated `if [ "${lrc}" -ne 0 ]` block (no `fi`) since #658. Every run that reached it died with `syntax error: unexpected end of file`, so the step whose own comment calls a silently unreported CVE "the worst outcome" has **never filed an issue** — while `main` carried an unreported HIGH (libexpat CVE-2026-93990) and `Base Image Freshness` was red daily from 2026-09-08. Fixed by hand in PR #757.

## Why it is a gate gap, not a one-off typo

Nothing in CI parses the shell inside a workflow's `run: |` blocks:

- `scripts/check-image-supply-chain.sh` parses this workflow's YAML and stayed green throughout — valid YAML, invalid bash.
- The step only executes on a **scheduled** scan failure, so no PR ever exercises it; every PR check was green across the whole period.
- Neither `actionlint` nor `shellcheck` is wired into any workflow (`git grep` finds only `shellcheck disable` comments).

## Evidence the check can fire

Splitting every `run: |` block into its own file and running `bash -n` on each (a 15-line awk + bash harness, no Python, recorded in PR #757):

- `main` @ `ed38eb82`: `base-image-freshness.yml` → **1 of 4 blocks fails**, `line 115: syntax error: unexpected end of file` (CI's log reports line 114 of the same block).
- After the fix: 0 of 4. Across all seven workflows: no other instance. Two workflows (`docs-freshness.yml`, `gitleaks.yml`) have only one-line `run:` steps, so the harness returns VOID for them, not clean — a real gate must treat "no blocks found" the same way.

## Smallest fix

A `scripts/check-workflow-shell-syntax.sh` gate (rc 0 / 1 / 2 = pass / syntax error / VOID), wired into an existing always-on job and registered with `check-gate-enforcement.sh`, shown failing on `ed38eb82`'s copy of the workflow before it is trusted. Alternatively `actionlint` with `shellcheck` on the runner, which also catches expression errors — but its shellcheck findings on the existing workflows would need triage first, so the `bash -n` gate is the zero-noise first step.
title: No CI check parses the shell inside workflow run: blocks — the freshness alert step was dead from #658 until #757 with every check green

body:
## What is red

The **Trivy image gate on `main` is failing** for the `core-java` image, as of run
[35770881104](https://github.com/Bralabee/JToye_OaaS_2026/actions/runs/35770881104)
(head `beb3ca79`, 2026-09-22). Exactly one finding:

```
Total: 1 (HIGH: 1, CRITICAL: 0)

│ com.rabbitmq:amqp-client (app.jar) │ CVE-2026-75516 │ HIGH │ fixed │ 5.33.1 │ 5.34.0 │
```

`edge-go` and `frontend` both passed. Every test and gate job in the run passed —
Run Tests, Integration Tests (Testcontainers RLS), Operational Contracts,
OpenAPI Breaking-Change Gate, Lint, Security Scan, MCP Server Tests, docs-freshness.
The pipeline's only failure is this image gate.

## It is time-based, not change-based

The pin was not touched. `rabbit-amqp-client.version = 5.33.1` was last modified on
**2026-08-24** by #657 (`e5a5e16a`), and nothing in `beb3ca79` goes near it —
that commit is the netty bump (#752) plus docs.

The last CI/CD Pipeline run on `main` before this one was **2026-09-07** (`e911ef58`),
and it was **green**. So `main` has had no push for 15 days, CVE-2026-75516 was
published into the vulnerability database in that window, and this run is simply the
first one to see it. The code did not change; the world did.

Recording that explicitly because the opposite reading — "the netty PR broke the image
gate" — is the natural one and is wrong.

## netty is clean, which is the positive control

The same scan output contains **zero** netty findings. CVE-2026-75595 and
CVE-2026-75596 do appear in the raw job log, but only inside the build-provenance
metadata echoing the commit subject — not in the findings table. So #752 did what it
claimed: the flagged jar is gone from the image, proven by the gate rather than by a
local hand-run.

## The fix

One line, exactly parallel to #657 and #752:

```
rabbit-amqp-client.version: 5.33.1 -> 5.34.0
```

`5.34.0` is the version Trivy itself names as fixed. Note the pin's existing comment —
this property is the one Spring Boot's BOM actually declares, and #657 exists because an
earlier attempt set a property that does not exist, so the value must be read back from
`dependencyInsight` rather than assumed to have applied.

## Why this is filed rather than noted

Per the admission test, a finding earns an issue when it **breaks a gate**. This one
does: `main`'s image gate is red and stays red until the pin moves. It is not a
"record it in the resolution comment" item.

## Context

Raised at the end of the 2026-09-22 session, which tore the local stack down for a
planned pause; the project resumes **2026-10-01**. Nothing is deployed from `main`
automatically, so the red gate is a merge-blocking and hygiene problem rather than a
live exposure — and the CVE is in a client library whose reachability has not been
assessed here.
title: Trivy image gate red on main: amqp-client 5.33.1 needs 5.34.0 for CVE-2026-75516

body:
## What

`check-dependency-horizons.sh` declares an exact `file:line` for each pin in
`infra/dependency-horizons.yaml` `sites:`. Four declared lines no longer match where the pin
actually sits, so the gate emits `pin-not-at-site=4` NOTEs on a clean tree:

```
NOTE ollama: pin not at docker-compose.full-stack.yml:621; found at line(s) 665,730 (run --refresh)
NOTE ollama: pin not at docker-compose.full-stack.yml:686; found at line(s) 665,730 (run --refresh)
NOTE mailhog: pin not at docker-compose.full-stack.yml:702; found at line(s) 746 (run --refresh)
NOTE go-ci-setup: pin not at .github/workflows/ci-cd.yaml:1269; found at line(s) 53,907,1272 (run --refresh)
```

**NOTE class, so nothing is at risk** — these cannot fail a build. The pins themselves are
correct; only the declared line numbers have drifted.

## Why now

Three of the four drifted **further because of #743**, whose comment block added ~22 lines above
them in the same file. #743 fixed its own two rows (`minio` 553→597, `minio-mc` 584→628/638) and
deliberately left these, because they are unrelated to a registry relocation and widening a PR that
was unblocking a dark nightly lane is the wrong trade. Recording the debt here so it is not simply
absorbed.

## Why it is not just `--refresh`

`--refresh` rewrites the declared line numbers from wherever the pin is currently found. That is
the right mechanism, but it needs its own verification, because a refresh can happily re-point a
site at a **plausible but wrong** line — a comment mentioning the pin, or a second occurrence —
and the result looks identical to a correct refresh. #743 demonstrated exactly this hazard from the
other direction: `MINIO_MC_IMAGE_REF` is a log string, not a pull site, yet it satisfies H-5's
file-wide search and can keep the gate quiet over a genuinely broken `image:` line.

So a refresh wants a bracket: run it, then for each changed site assert the new line is the
**pull site** (an `image:`/`docker run` line) and not a comment or a provenance echo, and confirm
`pin-not-at-site` drops to the expected count rather than merely changing. Expected outcome is
`pin-not-at-site=1` (the pre-existing `go-ci-setup` row, which should be diagnosed separately
rather than refreshed blind).

Note what the real output shows that a paraphrase hid: both `ollama` NOTEs report the SAME candidate
set `665,730`, because that pin legitimately appears twice (two services share the image), so a
refresh has to choose which declared site gets which line and cannot infer it. And `go-ci-setup`
offers **three** candidates — `53,907,1272` — which is precisely the plausible-but-wrong-line hazard
above, sitting in the output already.

## Suggested guard

A declared site drifting is inevitable whenever anyone edits a compose file, and a NOTE nobody
reads is how this accumulated to four. Worth considering whether the exact-line check earns its
keep at NOTE class at all, or whether it should either (a) be enforced, or (b) be replaced by a
"the pin appears exactly once on a non-comment line of this file" assertion that does not need
maintaining. Option (b) would have caught everything the line numbers were for, without drifting.

Raised by independent review of #743.
title: Four declared horizon sites have drifted from their pins (NOTE class), three of them further because of #743

body:
## The finding

`sharp` is not a declared dependency of the frontend. It appears in no dependency section of
`frontend/package.json` — it is an **overrides** entry:

```json
"overrides": { "sharp": "^0.35.0", "@auth/core": "0.41.3", "postcss": "^8.5.12", "nwsapi": "2.2.24" }
```

Meanwhile `next@16.3.4` declares `optionalDependencies.sharp: "^0.35.4"`.

So before #744, the installed `sharp` 0.35.3 **did not satisfy Next's own declared requirement**.
The tree was valid only because the root override held sharp below what Next asked for.

Measured:

```
frontend/package.json          overrides.sharp                     = ^0.35.0
                               (no sharp in dependencies,
                                devDependencies or optionalDependencies)
package-lock.json  node_modules/next  optionalDependencies.sharp   = ^0.35.4
```

## Why it matters going forward

The HIGH libheif advisory (GHSA-rgj7-g3m4-5g8c) made this visible; the override is what made it
possible. The next time a fix lands only in a version **outside** `^0.35.0` — say sharp 0.36 — this
override will silently cap the tree there, and `npm update` will not help, because npm is honouring
an instruction we gave it. The failure will look exactly like #744 did: Trivy red, no obvious cause
in the diff.

And nothing watches it:

- **Dependabot will not bump it.** It is not a declared dependency, so it is not in Dependabot's
  update surface.
- **`infra/dependency-horizons.yaml` does not track it.** That manifest covers images and
  toolchains; `rg -uu 'sharp' infra/ scripts/` returns **0** hits (control: the same scope returns 6
  for node/nodejs, so the search is live).
- Nothing asserts that the overrides block is still needed, or that each entry is still compatible
  with what its dependents declare.

## Suggested work

1. **Find out why the override exists.** `@auth/core`, `postcss` and `nwsapi` sit beside it, so
   there was probably a specific conflict. If the reason is gone, delete the entry and let Next's
   own `^0.35.4` govern — which is the outcome that needs no future maintenance.
2. If it must stay, **widen it deliberately** rather than by accident, and record why the ceiling is
   where it is.
3. **Add a check that every `overrides` entry is still satisfiable against its dependents'
   declared ranges**, so an override that has drifted below a dependent's floor fails loudly
   instead of being discovered through an unrelated CVE. Note that an override silently winning over
   a declared range is the generalisable defect here, not sharp specifically — `@auth/core` is
   pinned exactly, which has the same shape.

Found by independent review of #744. Not folded into that PR: #744 is a lockfile refresh whose job
was to clear a red gate, and removing or widening an override is a dependency-resolution change
needing its own reasoning and its own test run.
title: sharp is an overrides entry that held the tree below next's own declared range, and nothing tracks it

body:
## The problem

`docker-compose.full-stack.yml` resolves the MinIO bootstrap image as:

```yaml
minio-init:
  image: quay.io/minio/mc:${MINIO_MC_IMAGE_TAG:-latest}
```

That container holds the **ROOT** object-storage credentials, which is exactly why #270
digest-pinned it: a mutable tag would run whatever `latest` resolves to next, with full bucket
authority.

`.env.example` carries the pin (`RELEASE.2025-08-13T08-35-41Z@sha256:a7fe349e…`). **The local
`.env` declares neither `MINIO_MC_IMAGE_TAG` nor `MINIO_IMAGE_TAG`**, so on a developer machine the
`:-latest` fallback applies and the bootstrap runs an unpinned, mutable tag. Verified on the running
stack:

```
rg -uu -c 'MINIO_MC_IMAGE_TAG' .env        -> rc=1 (zero matches)
docker inspect jtoye-minio-init            -> .Config.Image = quay.io/minio/mc:latest
container log                              -> minio-init-image-ref=quay.io/minio/mc:latest
```

This is pre-existing and **CI is unaffected** — `.github/workflows/e2e-nightly.yml` copies
`.env.example`, which carries the digest.

## Why #743 makes it worth fixing now

Before the quay.io move, an absent variable failed **loudly**: `minio/mc:latest` on Docker Hub now
returns 401, so the stack simply would not start. After the move it returns **200**. The failure
mode flipped from "obvious breakage" to "a root-credentialed bootstrap silently runs a mutable tag",
which is the quieter and worse of the two.

## Suggested fix

Use a required-variable form rather than a silent fallback for the root-credentialed image:

```yaml
image: quay.io/minio/mc:${MINIO_MC_IMAGE_TAG:?MINIO_MC_IMAGE_TAG must be set (digest-pinned, see .env.example)}
```

**This is deliberately not folded into #743**, because on its own it would immediately break every
developer stack whose `.env` omits the variable — including the one in this repo's own working tree.
It needs to land together with:

1. adding `MINIO_MC_IMAGE_TAG` to `scripts/verify-env.sh` `REQUIRED_VARS`, so a missing value fails
   preflight rather than at container start;
2. a note in the local-setup docs that the value comes from `.env.example`;
3. the same decision for `MINIO_IMAGE_TAG` — the server image is not root-credentialed, so it may
   reasonably keep its fallback. Worth deciding explicitly rather than by omission.

Also note `MINIO_MC_IMAGE_REF` is echoed at run time precisely so a run states which image it ran —
that line is what made this visible, and it worked.

Found by independent review of #743.
title: minio-init's root-credentialed image silently falls back to a mutable tag when MINIO_MC_IMAGE_TAG is unset

body:
## What happened

`frontend/e2e/cart-identity-boundary.verify.mjs` is the executable guard for the
cart-identity boundary (context: #459 / R-16 — a basket must not cross a CUSTOMER
boundary, and must still cross an anonymous→signed-in one).

It located the storefront Add control with an anchored, case-insensitive exact match on
the single word "Add", at three sites. PR #726 gave that button an `aria-label` for
A11Y-4 / WCAG 2.4.6 — which is **correct** and must stay: nine cards on one page
exposed the identical accessible name "Add", and a name-driven actor added the wrong
dish. But `aria-label` REPLACES the accessible name, so the visible text "Add" stopped
being the name and the locator matched nothing.

Result: the nightly step `Gate — cart identity boundary (#459 / R-16)` was red at that
one step on five consecutive scheduled nights, 2026-09-07 through 2026-09-11, and on manual
dispatch 34401146291. (The 2026-09-12 run failed earlier, at the stack build, for an unrelated
reason.)
Every arm that SEEDS localStorage kept passing while both arms that CLICK a real Add
button timed out, so the run exited `VOID: expected at least 18 checks, got 9`. Two of
the guard's five criteria (C1 and C2) had not executed at all since 2026-09-07.

The locator itself is repaired on `feature/fix-cart-identity-add-locator`. **This issue
is about the decay mechanism, not the locator.**

## Mechanism

- **One of the four `frontend/e2e/*.verify.mjs` scripts runs in the nightly; the other three
  run in no lane at all.** Measured with `rg -uu`: four such files exist, and
  `.github/workflows/e2e-nightly.yml:419` is the single invocation anywhere in `.github/` or
  `scripts/`. The unrun three include `customer-signout-idp-session.verify.mjs`, which #726's
  own QA-council plan named as the regression oracle for the sign-out change it shipped
  (`.qa-council/20260902-134741/plan-frontend-a11y.md:203`) — an oracle that has never
  executed. This is a different severity from "thin coverage", and it is what makes an
  allow-list that enumerates every such file the right shape rather than a staleness detector
  for the one that runs.
- The one that does run is invoked in the nightly
  (`.github/workflows/e2e-nightly.yml`), invoked directly as
  `node --env-file=.env frontend/e2e/cart-identity-boundary.verify.mjs` — **not** via
  `playwright test`. No PR ever exercises them.
- Nothing ties their `getByRole(..., { name: /…/ })` patterns to the accessible names
  the component actually renders.
- So #726 updated the `*.spec.ts` specs and the jsdom tests — which ARE run on a PR —
  and missed this file. Five nightlies plus one manual dispatch burned before anyone
  looked.

A guard nothing executes decays without anyone learning it decayed. That is the defect
worth addressing; the dead locator was only its first symptom.

## Rejected, deliberately: the obvious grep gate

"Assert that no anchored exact-match-on-Add locator survives under `frontend/e2e/`" is
a **deny-list**, and a deny-list guard fails OPEN. It catches the one spelling that
already bit us and is blind to every next rename: `aria-label` → `aria-labelledby`, a
reworded label, a title change, a new control.

It is also not "a few lines". Any new `scripts/check-*.sh` must be wired into a
workflow, or `scripts/check-gate-enforcement.sh` reds the build for being unwired.

Not implemented.

## Worth costing — two allow-list candidates

**(a) One shared exported locator constant.** A single constant consumed by both
`storefront-dish-modal-a11y.spec.ts` and `cart-identity-boundary.verify.mjs`, so a
rename has ONE site and a missing export is a load-time error rather than a silent
zero-match. Cheap. Narrows the blast radius, but on its own still does not detect a
component-side rename.

**(b) A jsdom-render assertion over the e2e locators.** Assert that every
accessible-name pattern used under `frontend/e2e/` resolves against the names the
component actually renders. This is the only shape that fails **closed**: when the
component's label changes, the assertion goes red on the very PR that changes it.
`frontend/__tests__/shop/server-seeded-islands.test.tsx` already demonstrates the
technique for this one component. It needs a way to enumerate the patterns, which is
what (a) provides — so (a) is a prerequisite, not an alternative.

## Context

- #459 — the cart-identity boundary this guard exists to protect (R-16).
- #726 — the PR whose correct accessibility change the stale locator failed to follow.
- Nightly runs 2026-09-07 / 09-08 / 09-09 / 09-10 / 09-11 and dispatch 34401146291 — the
  six red runs, every one of them red at this same step.
title: e2e: the *.verify.mjs nightly gates decay silently — no PR runs them, and nothing ties their locators to the names the component renders

body:
## Summary

`SyncService.upsertProduct` never sets `shopId`, and `SyncItem` carries no field that could supply one. A product created through `POST /api/v1/sync/batch` therefore lands with `shop_id = NULL` — attached to no shop, and invisible on every storefront surface, which lists per shop.

The insert **succeeds**. `products.shop_id` has been nullable since V20 (`ALTER TABLE products ADD COLUMN shop_id UUID REFERENCES shops(id) ON DELETE SET NULL`), so nothing rejects it and nothing logs it.

## Evidence (measured 2026-09-04)

- `rg -uu 'setShopId' core-java/src/main/java/uk/jtoye/core/sync/SyncService.java` → no match. Control: three other files in `core-java/src/main/java` do call it, so the pattern is matchable.
- `SyncItem` (`core-java/src/main/java/uk/jtoye/core/sync/dto/SyncItem.java`) declares exactly: `type, sku, title, ingredientsText, allergenMask, pricePennies, name, address`. `name`/`address` are the **shop** fields. There is no product-level shop reference of any kind.
- `products.shop_id` nullable per `V20__per_shop_products_and_inventory.sql:6`.
- The update path is unaffected — an existing product keeps whatever `shop_id` it already had.

## Severity: latent, not live

`POST /sync/batch` still has **no production producer**. Re-measured today, not inherited from #648's 2026-08-19 measurement: `rg -uu 'sync/batch'` over `frontend/`, `mcp-server/` and `scripts/` returns nothing, and the only non-doc references are `core-java` and `edge-go` itself. So no orphaned products exist from this route today.

That is exactly why it deserves filing rather than fixing quietly: the defect is invisible until someone wires the first producer, and then it is silent.

## This is not a regression from #726

`git show origin/main:core-java/src/main/java/uk/jtoye/core/sync/SyncService.java` has no `setShopId` either. #726 hardened the **authorization** on this endpoint (SEC-5/API-1, the fix for #648) and did not introduce or worsen the binding gap. It did make it more visible: the new access check reads
`shopAccessService.require(existing.map(Product::getShopId).orElse(null), ShopRole.SHOP_MANAGER)`
— i.e. the code now reasons explicitly about a null shop binding on the create path, while nothing ever supplies one.

## Why this shape matters

It is the same class as API-13, fixed in the sibling function twelve lines above in the same file: *"a bare `shopRepository.save(new Shop())` never set `slug` (NOT NULL), so this branch had failed on every attempt (zero rows ever)"*.

Products are the **worse** version of that bug. Shops failed loudly against a `NOT NULL` and were eventually noticed. Products succeed against a nullable column and produce a row that looks fine in the table and appears nowhere in the product.

## What needs deciding before it can be fixed

This is a design call, not a one-line change:

1. **How does a sync item name its shop?** A `shopSlug` or `shopName` on `SyncItem` is the obvious candidate — slug is stable, name is already the shop upsert key, and picking one determines whether product sync can reference a shop created earlier in the same batch.
2. **What happens to an existing orphan on re-sync?** Adopt it into the named shop, or leave it alone? Adoption silently rewrites history for a row a vendor may never have seen.
3. **Should the binding be mandatory?** If yes, an unbound product item should be rejected with a typed RFC 7807 error rather than skipped, and `products.shop_id` arguably wants a NOT NULL once the data supports it.
4. **Does the access check tighten?** With a real shop to scope to, product creation could move from GROUP_ADMIN-only to `require(shopId, SHOP_MANAGER)` — closing the last place `/sync/batch` write access is coarser than the dashboard's.

Per this repo's standard, the deny/orphan test should be written and **observed failing** before any fix lands.

## Related

- #648 — the authorization half of this endpoint (fixed in #726). Read together, but distinct: #648 is who may write, this is what the write produces.
- #109 — sync batch upsert race, no unique constraint on `shops.name`/`products.sku`. Touches the same upsert keys and would likely be resolved by the same design pass.

Found during a read-only review pass on #726.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

https://claude.ai/code/session_01VH4MN2z7JZCfiRZxXVScrS
title: Sync-created products are orphaned: upsertProduct never sets shop_id and SyncItem cannot supply one

body:
## Why this issue exists

`scripts/check-dependency-horizons.sh` (the **Operational Contracts** CI job) turned red on every PR on **2026-09-02** with no code change:

```
FAIL: H-3 rabbitmq: rabbitmq/4.3 approaching 2026-11-30 (vendor (eol_source override), 89 days)
```

This is the amber-with-no-commit moment the gate's own header predicted ("At the default 90-day window this job turns AMBER ~2026-09-01 ... Intended. Not an outage. Not a broken gate."). The manifest row `rabbitmq` in `infra/dependency-horizons.yaml` now carries a dated `exemption:` that names this issue as `tracked_by`, so the gate is green **only until 2026-11-30**. On **2026-12-01** the exemption expires AND the row is past EOL, and Operational Contracts reds every PR again. That is the treadmill working as designed; this issue is the work that steps off it.

## Measured on 2026-09-02

| Fact | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Pinned image | `rabbitmq:4.3.4-management-alpine` | `docker-compose.full-stack.yml` |
| Latest 4.3 patch | 4.3.5 (released 17 Aug 2026) | rabbitmq.com/release-information |
| 4.3 end of community support | **30 Nov 2026** | rabbitmq.com/release-information |
| 4.3 end of commercial support | 30 Apr 2028 (none held) | rabbitmq.com/release-information |
| Newest cycle in the catalogue | 4.3 (`eol: false`, `latest: 4.3.5`) | endoflife.date/api/rabbitmq.json |
| 4.4 GA | **not released** — no 4.4 cycle, no `rabbitmq:4.4*` tag on Docker Hub (only `3.4.4`) | endoflife.date + hub.docker.com |

So there is no upgrade target today. Historical cadence (4.0 Sep 2024, 4.1 Apr 2025, 4.2 Oct 2025, 4.3 Apr 2026) puts 4.4 around Oct 2026, which leaves roughly one month inside the window.

## What to do (when 4.4 GA ships)

1. Read the version off the **running** broker first, per `docs/runbooks/rabbitmq-broker-upgrade.md` §1 — the compose file states an intent, only the broker states a fact.
2. Confirm from the 4.4 release notes that 4.3 → 4.4 is an in-place upgrade (unlike 3.12 → 4.x, which had no Mnesia reader and was done by fresh install). Enable any required feature flags on 4.3 before switching the image.
3. Bump the pin in `docker-compose.full-stack.yml` (currently line 224; the manifest `sites:` entry drifted from 149 and is refreshed in the same PR that files this issue).
4. Update the manifest row: `pin`, `eol_cycle: "4.4"`, `vendor_eol`, and **remove the exemption block** — H-4 fails an exemption on a row that is no longer inside the window (STALE), so leaving it would itself be a violation.
5. Rebuild the stack (`compose start` does not rebuild), run the Playwright suite, and read the version back off the broker.
6. The staging/production broker is not deployed from this repo (ADR-0002; manifest row `rabbitmq-k8s`, `owner: UNASSIGNED`). Its version is unverifiable from here and this issue does not cover it.

## Interim option (not taken in the filing PR)

A patch bump 4.3.4 → 4.3.5 is available now. It does not move the horizon (same 30 Nov 2026 date) and it is a runtime change requiring a rebuild + E2E, so it was deliberately left out of the gate-unblock PR that was opened right before a QA council remediation round. Fold it into this upgrade, or do it on its own if 4.4 slips.

## Acceptance

- Running broker reports 4.4.x (`docker exec jtoye-rabbitmq rabbitmqctl version`).
- `bash scripts/check-dependency-horizons.sh` exits 0 with **no** exemption on the `rabbitmq` row.
- Playwright suite green on the rebuilt stack; `scripts/check-runtime-freshness.sh` 4/4.

Found by the 2026-08-31 housekeeping full-suite runs (two consecutive, reproducible after a clean `seed-e2e-fixtures.sh` rc=0): `onboarding-blocked-flow.spec.ts` ONBD-05 fails at its final assertion (`getByText(/with our team for review/i)` — 60s timeout, element not found) with 316 passed / 6 skipped otherwise stable.

The failure screenshot shows the demo tenant at **"Ready to go live" — Submitted ✓, Approved ✓ (1 day ago), "Went live · pending"** — parked there by the #690 approvals-queue ratification on 2026-08-30. That state falls between two predicates:

1. The spec's own skip-guard recognizes only `Your storefront is live|withdrawn|suspended|wasn't approved` — APPROVED/ready-to-go-live matches none, so it proceeds instead of skipping.
2. `seed-e2e-fixtures.sh` section 3 (the #686/#693 fix) resets the row only when **LIVE/terminal** — APPROVED-but-not-yet-live is neither, so the reseed leaves it in place.

So the blocked journey runs against a tenant whose state machine can never reach in-review. The nightly is immune (`down -v` fresh volume), which is why it stays green while any local checkout that has ratified an approval reds this spec forever until someone hand-resets the row.

Fix shape (same falsification discipline as #693): extend the seeder's reset predicate to include the APPROVED/ready-to-go-live state (vendor tenant only, `Shop.published` untouched — note going live is exactly what the reset must NOT trigger), AND/OR extend the spec's skip-guard regex to recognize the ready-to-go-live copy as a skip-with-declared-reason. Whichever is chosen, both arms observed failing first: current APPROVED row → spec red (banked in this issue), post-reset → full journey passes (the #693 arm), and the skip-budget gate stays within budget with the skip declared if the guard route is taken.

Evidence: two full-suite runs 2026-08-31 (~17:37 and ~18:0x UTC), failure artifact `frontend/test-results/onboarding-blocked-flow-*/test-failed-1.png`, seed rc=0 immediately before the second run.

Related: #686 (the original undeclared-skip cause), PR #693 (the LIVE/terminal reset), #690 (the ratification that parked the tenant at APPROVED).
title: seed-e2e-fixtures + ONBD-05 both miss the APPROVED onboarding state — blocked-journey spec fails locally against a ready-to-go-live tenant

The PR #715 review (`.planning/quick/260831-lxf-fix-r-16-anonymous-downgrade-cart-leak-c/260831-lxf-REVIEW.md`, WR-06) found that `cart-identity-boundary.verify.mjs` — the guard for the R-16 cart-ownership leak — ran in NO workflow, gate script, or npm script, and had silently decayed twice while unwired (a Tailwind class move killed 5 of its arms via a 30s locator timeout; the Phase-31 allergen gate broke its checkout arm). PR #715 wired that one script into e2e-nightly by hand. The CLASS stays open:

1. Three sibling `frontend/e2e/*.verify.mjs` guards still run nowhere (measured by `rg -uu` across `.github/`, `scripts/`, `package.json` — among them `customer-signout-idp-session.verify.mjs`). Each is a boundary guard someone wrote after a real defect, currently decoration.
2. `check-gate-enforcement.sh` is structurally blind to the class: it inventories `scripts/check-*.sh` at maxdepth 1 only (measured negative, both directions, in the 260831-lxf plan and re-confirmed in the review). So a verify script can be added, cited in docs, and never execute — with no gate able to notice.

Per the proof-standards doctrine, the fix is a script that fails loudly, not a firmer instruction: either extend `check-gate-enforcement.sh`'s inventory to cover `frontend/e2e/*.verify.mjs` (with the same exemption-table mechanics), or add a dedicated `scripts/check-verify-script-wiring.sh` that fails when a `.verify.mjs` exists with no executable reference — shown to FAIL on a deliberately orphaned fixture before being trusted. Wiring the three scripts themselves needs the same fixture-impact review WR-04 documented for the cart guard (real Keycloak registrations, real orders).

Related: #714 (the same unwired-gate shape for the Keycloak theme contract, from PR #713's review).

## What

`/dashboard/onboarding/approvals` carries the **Index** tier (fluid to the ~1700px shell cap).
Plan 35-04 recorded this as **the phase's lowest-confidence tier call** (marker `A-8` at the
site) and routed it to the 35-13 owner gate for an explicit answer. The gate could not give
one, and the reason is measurable rather than an oversight.

## Why it could not be decided

Measured on the delivered runtime (phase 35 branch, `check-runtime-freshness.sh` 4/4 FRESH),
`--project=desktop`, at three viewports:

| viewport | index band | table | rows |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1440 | 1120px | none | 0 |
| 1920 | 1600px | none | 0 |
| 2560 | 1636px | none | 0 |

The page renders its **empty state** on the seeded stack:

> "No applications waiting — Applications appear here when their compliance checks pass and a
> human…"

So there is no row, card or heading to judge. The defect class the gate exists to catch on
this surface — content hugging the left edge of a now-wider band, or a heading stranded alone
across a wide row — **cannot appear on an empty queue**, and a green look at it would be a
vacuous pass, not an approval.

This is the same root cause as #686: the demo tenant's onboarding is in a LIVE/terminal state,
which is also why `onboarding-blocked-flow.spec.ts` skips and puts the skip budget at 7/6.

## What would settle it

A seeded PENDING approval — one application whose compliance checks have passed and which is
waiting on a human decision. With one row on screen, the Index-vs-Detail call is a five-second
look at 2560px. Without one it is undecidable at any width.

Note this is an **additive** follow-up, not a defect in what shipped: Index was chosen
deliberately and the reason is written at the call site. Phase 35 explicitly declined to
apply the alternative on a hunch. Retiering is a one-line change plus its manifest row in
`docs/architecture/layout-tiers.tsv`.

## Related

- Phase 35, plan 35-04 (marker A-8), plan 35-13 (the owner gate)
- #686 — the same terminal-state seed that empties this queue
- #683 — the dark nightly lane, which is why no browser on any current tree measures this band

## Also measured at the gate, and recorded here so it is not re-raised on a hunch

The gate's other named additive candidate was "the finance chart band" — its step 3 told the
owner that `/dashboard/finance` "has charts above its table" and that stretching them could
read worse. **That premise is false.** `/dashboard/finance` renders **zero** charts at 1440,
1920 and 2560, and the page source imports no chart library at all; the selector control found
2 charts on `/dashboard` in the same run, so the zero is about the page and not about the
probe. The real charts are on the `/dashboard` overview (Shell tier) and their aspect ratio
goes 1.99 (498x250 @1440) -> 2.95 (738x250 @1920) -> 3.02 (756x250 @2560) — bounded by the
1700px shell cap, and 3:1 is an ordinary dashboard chart proportion. That candidate is
therefore closed as moot by measurement, not deferred.
title: Approvals queue tier (Index vs Detail) is undecidable while the queue renders empty — phase 35's lowest-confidence call

body:
## Summary

The per-PR `jest-axe` dashboard gate added in #685 (finding A11Y-5 / escalation E1) **cannot evaluate the `scrollable-region-focusable` rule**. That rule is runtime-geometric, and jsdom has no layout engine, so the check passes vacuously for it. This does not make the gate useless — it is real for the rules it can evaluate — but the A11Y-3 fix it appears to protect is **not** actually gated per-PR.

## Proof (both directions, measured on this tree)

axe-core 4.13.0, `node_modules/axe-core/axe.js:19610-19613`:

```js
function getScroll(elm) {
  var buffer = ... : 0;
  var overflowX = elm.scrollWidth > elm.clientWidth + buffer;
  var overflowY = elm.scrollHeight > elm.clientHeight + buffer;
  if (!(overflowX || overflowY)) {
    return;            // <-- rule never applies
  }
```

The rule therefore requires real layout. In jsdom, an element that genuinely overflows in a browser reports zero for both:

```
$ node -e "...jsdom: <div style='overflow-x:auto;width:100px'><table style='width:5000px'>..."
scrollWidth= 0  clientWidth= 0
overflowX would be: false
```

So `getScroll` returns early and `scrollable-region-focusable` is never assessed under jsdom, for any element, regardless of markup.

## Why this matters

- #685's A11Y-3 fix made the dashboard `overflow-x-auto` region keyboard-reachable (`tabIndex=0` + accessible name). The Jest counterpart asserts the **attribute is present** — which stays green whether or not the region still overflows, and whether or not the name is still correct in a real layout.
- The functional counterpart lives in the **nightly** `dashboard-a11y-nightly.spec.ts`, which is **report-only** and runs in `e2e-nightly.yml` — the lane currently dark per #683. So the only instrument that can actually evaluate this rule is neither blocking nor running.

Net: for this rule specifically, we have an attribute check that cannot fail for the right reason, and a browser check that does not block and is not running.

## Suggested resolution

1. Document, in `frontend/__tests__/dashboard-a11y-axe.test.tsx`, which axe rules are structurally unevaluable under jsdom, so nobody reads a green there as coverage of them. (Geometric rules: `scrollable-region-focusable`, and anything else depending on layout boxes.)
2. Move the geometric a11y assertions to a **blocking** browser context, or at minimum restore the nightly lane (#683) and make the region check blocking there.
3. Consider asserting the property directly in a browser spec — focusability of the scroll container measured with real `scrollWidth`/`clientWidth` — rather than relying on axe to reach it.

## Provenance

Found while researching Phase 35 (horizontal layout contract), which changes when the dashboard scroll region overflows and therefore needed to know which instrument actually guards it. Related: #683 (nightly lane dark), #686 (skip-budget gate only runs in that dark lane).
title: jest-axe dashboard gate cannot evaluate scrollable-region-focusable (geometric rule, jsdom has no layout) — A11Y-3 is ungated per-PR

## Summary

#685's F2 cluster (FEB-1) correctly replaced the false-zero empty state with an honest error panel. Two smaller instances of the same class survive on `/dashboard/products` when the catalogue load fails.

Verified in a real browser against the post-#685 runtime (all 4 images FRESH), by stubbing `GET /api/v1/products**` to 500. The check was run in **both directions** — with the stub the error panel renders; without it the same assertions fail — so it is falsifiable.

## What is right

The main fix works: "Couldn't load products / Something went wrong loading this data. Please try again." + a **Try again** button, and "No products yet" is correctly absent.

## Residual 1 — the count label still asserts a false zero

The card header still reads **"0 products in total"** while the panel simultaneously says the data could not load. That is a smaller version of the exact defect FEB-1 fixed: a number presented as fact when nothing was loaded. A vendor glancing at the header can still read "0" as their catalogue.

Suggested: suppress or dash out the count when `loadError` is set, e.g. render "—" or omit the subtitle entirely.

## Residual 2 — the toast still shows raw axios text

The toast reads **"Request failed with status code 500"**. The panel copy is humanised via `lib/human-error.ts`, but the toast on this surface is not routed through it — which is the same raw-string problem A11Y-2 fixed on the orders page.

Suggested: route the products toast through the shared `human-error` helper so panel and toast agree and neither leaks transport detail.

## Scope note

Both are low severity and neither reintroduces the original defect. Worth checking the other four swept surfaces (`orders`, `customers`, `shops`, `/shop`) for the same two edges, since the helper was applied consistently but the count label and toast were per-page.

Found during post-merge E2E verification of #685.
title: Products error state: header still says '0 products in total' and toast shows raw axios text (residual FEB-1 edges)

## Summary

`e2e/marketing-motion.spec.ts` › "mobile floor (375px) — no heavy scenes" › **"/ degrades to fully-visible static content"** is flaky. With `retries: 0` in `playwright.config.ts`, it will randomly red CI.

## Measured flakiness

`--repeat-each=3` across both projects (12 test instances):

```
2 failed, 10 passed (2.3m)
  [mobile]  › / degrades to fully-visible static content
  [desktop] › / degrades to fully-visible static content
```

Both failures are on `/`. The sibling path `/for-operators` passed every time.

Failing assertion (`marketing-motion.spec.ts:127`):

```
expect(await page.locator(".gsap-word").count()).toBe(0)
```

At a 375px viewport the landing page intermittently builds a GSAP scene that the mobile-floor contract says must not exist.

## It is NOT caused by #685

- The only change #685 made to `frontend/app/page.tsx` is `<head>` metadata (`alternates.canonical` + `openGraph`) for FE-5.
- `git diff b2c01600 96c8d794 --name-only` contains **no motion/GSAP source file**. `.gsap-word` is owned by `frontend/components/marketing/hero-scene.tsx`, untouched.
- It passed two full local suite runs and the PR's own CI E2E job before failing on repeat.

So this is pre-existing, and surfaced only because the test was run repeatedly.

## Likely mechanism (unconfirmed)

The spec waits `networkidle` + 500ms then counts. If the hero scene mounts before the viewport/media-query gate settles and tears down afterwards, the count is a race. Worth fixing at the source (do not build the scene below the breakpoint) rather than by extending the wait, which would only widen the race window.

Found during post-merge E2E verification of #685.
title: Flaky E2E: marketing-motion '/ degrades to fully-visible static content' fails ~1 in 3 (retries=0, will red CI)

## Summary

The E2E skip-budget gate (`scripts/check-e2e-skip-budget.sh`) **fails on the current tree**, and the only place it runs is `e2e-nightly.yml` — the lane that is dark (#683). Nothing has been enforcing it.

## Evidence (local, against the post-#685 runtime, 4/4 images FRESH)

```
tests     : 301 total, 7 skipped (budget 6)
FAIL: S-1 7 skipped test(s) exceeds the declared budget of 6
FAIL: S-2 undeclared skip: "onboarding-blocked-flow.spec.ts › bad company number ->
      fix inline -> re-run checks -> honest in-review @desktop-only"
declared  : 2 ALLOW entr(ies), 4 distinct skipped title(s)
S-4 self  : matcher fires on a known title and declines a constructed-absent one
```

The gate self-tests (S-4), so the FAIL is trustworthy.

## Why it skips

Not a credential problem (the vendor password mints a token fine). The recorded Playwright annotation is:

> Target tenant onboarding is already LIVE/terminal — this blocked-journey spec needs a fresh/disposable tenant. Skipping to avoid failing against or mutating the live demo.

That is sound reasoning by the spec. The consequence is that a **Phase 21 blocked-onboarding journey (ONBD-05) is silently unexercised**, and because the enforcing gate lives only in the dark nightly lane, no signal was ever raised.

## Skip inventory (7)

- `stomp-relay.spec.ts` x4 — declared ALLOW, gated on `RELAY_E2E` (multi-replica stack)
- `vendor-refund-flow.spec.ts` x2 — declared ALLOW, needs real `STRIPE_API_KEY`
- `onboarding-blocked-flow.spec.ts` x1 — **undeclared**, tenant-state dependent

## Suggested resolution (needs a decision, not just a config edit)

1. Give the blocked-onboarding spec a **fresh/disposable tenant fixture** so it runs rather than skips (preferred — restores real coverage), or
2. Declare it in `scripts/gates/e2e-skip-budget.conf` with a justification and raise `MAX_SKIPS`, which is the weaker option because it converts lost coverage into an accepted constant.

Separately: the skip-budget gate should arguably run somewhere that is not dark. Tracked-adjacent: #683.

Found during post-merge E2E verification of #685.

**Class:** the V64 class — "a provisioning step only a human can perform is not provisioning". Found by Phase 34's closeout (PR #682, plan 34-10), which needed a genuinely fresh volume.

**Measured, on a fresh volume** (`docker compose down -v` then `up -d`):

```
core-java: FATAL: password authentication failed for user "jtoye_app"   (SQL state 28P01)
           Flyway -> Unable to obtain connection from database
           container state: Restarting (1) — crash-looping, zero migrations applied
```

**Root cause** (read out of the two sources, not guessed): `infra/db/init/00-create-db.sql:44` creates `jtoye_app` with `DB_PASSWORD`, but since the SEC-04/#552 runtime-migrator split `DB_MIGRATION_USER=jtoye_app` and Flyway authenticates with `DB_MIGRATION_PASSWORD` (the same file says so at :56). When the two credentials differ, the role is created with a password Flyway does not know. Compared by digest only: `04897cf1…` vs `0bdf4558…` — different. The script's own :42-43 comment ("core-java connects as jtoye_app with DB_PASSWORD") is stale — `DB_USER` is now `jtoye_runtime`.

**Why it was invisible:** the long-lived local volume predates the split, so its `jtoye_app` already carried a working password; only destroying the volume exposes it. CI is unaffected wherever the two variables are generated equal. The nightly's `down -v` is the surface most at risk.

**Environment unblock applied (no committed file changed):** `ALTER ROLE jtoye_app PASSWORD` to the migration credential, verified by actually authenticating as `jtoye_app`; core-java then reached healthy and Flyway applied V1..V64.

**Fix + close condition** (from `.planning/phases/34-rendering-test-truthfulness/deferred-items.md` D-34-10-08): `00-create-db.sql:44` creates `jtoye_app` with `DB_MIGRATION_PASSWORD` (falling back to `DB_PASSWORD` only when unset, so single-credential setups keep working), the stale :42-43 comment corrected, and the fix proven on a `down -v` cycle where the two credentials deliberately DIFFER — the arm this defect needs, and the one nobody has run.
title: A fresh volume cannot provision itself: 00-create-db.sql creates jtoye_app with the wrong credential since the SEC-04 split (28P01 crash-loop, zero migrations)

The scheduled full-stack Playwright run failed. This lane is the project's
**only** full-suite E2E instrument, so while it is red **no merge has
full-suite evidence on any tree**.

### Triage, in order

1. **Did the stack come up at all?** The common failure is that core-java
   never becomes healthy, so Playwright never runs and no `report.json` is
   produced. Check the `Wait for core-java and the frontend` step first — if
   it timed out, this is a stack problem, not a test problem.
2. **Read the container logs in the `Dump stack logs on failure` step.** Note
   it runs `docker compose logs --tail 400`, so a crash-looping container's
   FIRST failure may be truncated out. If the tail looks like a clean
   shutdown, look for a repeating error earlier.
3. **A fresh volume is not the developer's machine.** `Tear down` runs
   `down -v`, so every night starts from an empty database and only
   `infra/db/init/00-create-db.sql` has run. Anything requiring a manual
   provisioning step will work locally and fail here every single night —
   that was #647.
4. **If Playwright DID run**, the failure is a real test regression: pull the
   uploaded report artifact and read the verdict from `report.json`.

### Do not

Do not close this because a re-run went green without a code change — an
intermittent nightly is still a lane you cannot trust. Close it when you know
which change fixed it.

**Run:** https://github.com/Bralabee/JToye_OaaS_2026/actions/runs/33228145134

**Commit:** `896c88283b90bb9e649c5153f8c1b3f67e3ecf03`

body:
## Summary

`docker-compose.full-stack.yml` publishes core-java as a **port range**:

    ports:
      - "9090-9091:9090"    # Replica 1 -> localhost:9090, Replica 2 -> localhost:9091

With a single replica, Docker allocates from the range non-deterministically. Measured
2026-08-28: the container landed on host **9091** with **9090 completely free** (`ss -ltnp`
showed no listener). Meanwhile the frontend bundle bakes
`NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL: http://localhost:9090` at **build time** (compose build arg), so every
browser-side API call hits a port with nothing behind it.

## Why it presents as product bugs, not as a config problem

Server-side rendering is unaffected - it uses the in-network `core-java:9090` - so **pages
load perfectly** and only client-side calls fail. The storefront renders, the menu renders,
and then checkout reports "Failed to place order. Please try again."

Measured cost on 2026-08-28: **six tests failed locally** that pass in CI (`:136` search
plus the five postcode-proximity tests), and the checkout POST failed with HTTP 000. All
six went green after:

    docker compose -f docker-compose.full-stack.yml up -d --force-recreate --no-deps core-java

which happened to land the container on 9090 - **with no code change**, which is what
identifies the port allocation as the cause rather than the product.

This same mechanism plausibly contributed to earlier confusing local E2E sessions; CI never
sees it because the nightly starts from a fresh project where allocation starts at the
bottom of the range.

## Options

1. Pin the single-replica case to `"9090:9090"` and make the range an override file or a
   profile used only when actually scaling replicas.
2. Keep the range but add a preflight to `scripts/start-dev.sh` / `seed-e2e-fixtures.sh`
   that asserts a listener on the port the frontend bundle was built against, failing
   loudly with the recreate command.
3. Both - the pin fixes the default, the preflight catches any future divergence between
   the baked `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` and the published port.

The check must be shown to fail (stack on 9091) before it is trusted.

Surfaced while fixing #666 (PR #670); full measurement in
`.planning/quick/20260828-e2e-storefront-nightly-six/SUMMARY.md`.
title: Compose publishes core-java on a port RANGE (9090-9091) while the frontend bundle bakes localhost:9090 — browser-side calls silently die when Docker picks 9091

body:
`ci-cd.yaml` derives the image owner from `github.repository_owner` in two places and then
pins it as a **lowercase literal** in twelve others. The two halves disagree the moment the
owner changes.

### Where

Derived:
- `.github/workflows/ci-cd.yaml:13` — `IMAGE_PREFIX: ${{ github.repository_owner }}/jtoye`
- `.github/workflows/ci-cd.yaml:1036` — `images: ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ env.IMAGE_PREFIX }}-${{ matrix.service }}`

Hardcoded `ghcr.io/bralabee/...`:
- staging deploy — lines 1235-1237, and the premortem grep at 1244-1247
- production deploy — lines 1359-1361, and the premortem grep at 1368-1371

### Why it matters

On a fork, an org transfer or a rename, `build-and-push` publishes to the **new** owner
(metadata-action derives it) while `kustomize edit set image` still targets
`ghcr.io/bralabee/...`. The premortem grep at 1244 then fires `FATAL` and both deploy jobs
fail with a reference that no rebuild can fix — the image exists, just not under that name.

It is also the same class as #658: an image reference assembled from an owner that is not
handled consistently. #658 fixed the hand-built reference in `base-image-freshness.yml` and
added `X-6` to `scripts/check-image-supply-chain.sh` to keep it fixed. This is the same
defect one layer down, and `X-6` does not cover `ci-cd.yaml`.

It also violates the project's standing config rule — never hardcode values that vary by
environment.

### Suggested fix

Compute a lowercased image base **once** and consume it in both files, so
`base-image-freshness.yml` and `ci-cd.yaml` cannot drift from each other or from the registry.
Extend `X-6` to assert `ci-cd.yaml` carries no hardcoded owner literal, so the fix cannot
silently revert.

### Not urgent

Nothing is broken today: the repo owner is `Bralabee`, the literal `bralabee` is its correct
lowercase form, and the deploy jobs work. This is latent, and it bites exactly when someone
forks or renames — i.e. when they are least able to diagnose it.

Found by code review on #658.
title: ci-cd.yaml hardcodes the image owner in 12 places while deriving it in 2 — a fork or rename breaks both deploy jobs

## Summary

`POST /api/v1/sync/batch` (`SyncController` → `SyncService`) is gated by **`anyRequest().authenticated()` only** — no scope, no role, no `@PreAuthorize`, and **no `ShopAccessService` check**. Any authenticated tenant staff member scoped to shop A can create/mutate **any** shop or product within their tenant, bypassing the Phase-23 second wall that gates the normal Shop/Product write paths.

The RLS tenant wall **holds** — the attacker-controlled `tenantId` in the request body is never read; `SyncService` takes the tenant solely from `TenantContext` and writes under the RLS GUC, so there is **no cross-tenant reach**. The gap is **intra-tenant, write-side**.

## Evidence (measured 2026-08-19)

- `SecurityConfig`: `/api/v1/sync/**` falls under `anyRequest().authenticated()` — no dedicated rule.
- `SyncService.processBatch` upserts via `shopRepository`/`productRepository` directly, with no `ShopAccessService.require(...)` anywhere in the `sync` package. It does **not** touch `Shop.published` (state-machine sole-writer invariant intact).
- The only test is `SyncControllerIntegrationTest`, a `@WebMvcTest` with **`addFilters = false`** and a mocked service — i.e. **zero authorization coverage and no deny-test**.
- Live caller: `edge-go/cmd/edge/main.go:304` forwards the caller's own token to this route — but there is **no production producer** today (`rg -uu 'sync/batch'` over frontend/scripts/mcp → none), so the edge's only protected route currently has no live caller.

## Why it matters

This is the same class as **FC-1** (a shipped cross-tenant write BOLA behind an accepted surface) — a write path that skips the intra-tenant authorization boundary the rest of the write surface enforces. Not an emergency (no cross-tenant reach; caller must hold a valid tenant JWT), but it should not stay unfixed and untested.

## Recommended actions

**Decide the endpoint's intent, then add the deny-test FIRST and watch it fail:**
1. Restrict `/sync/batch` to a dedicated machine scope/role; **or**
2. Route its writes through `ShopAccessService`; **or**
3. Retire `/sync` (it has no production caller — the "offline edge devices" story is aspirational).

In all three cases, add a negative (deny) integration test that exercises real security filters, proven to fail before the fix.

Documented in `docs/FAILURE_MODES.md` §0 (F-0.2). Surfaced by the 2026-08-19 system tour.
title: Within-tenant BOLA: POST /api/v1/sync/batch bypasses shop-scoping and has zero authz test coverage

## Summary

The `e2e-nightly.yml` full-stack Playwright suite — the project's **only** full-suite E2E instrument — has failed **9 consecutive scheduled nights** (2026-08-11 → 2026-08-19). The compose stack never becomes healthy, so Playwright never runs and **no `report.json` has been produced since 2026-08-10**. **Nothing alerts on it.**

Every merge since 2026-08-10 — including the Phase 31 merge (#633, 18 plans) and #634 — has therefore landed with **zero full-suite E2E evidence on any tree**. This is also the underlying cause of the standing `check-e2e-skip-budget` VOID (the spec digest can only refresh from a completed nightly).

## Evidence (measured 2026-08-19)

- `gh run list --workflow=e2e-nightly.yml`: last success **2026-08-10 02:45 UTC** (run 31350659698); 9 failures since, each dying in 5–11 min.
- Failure mode: `dependency failed to start: container jtoye_oaas_2026-core-java-1 is unhealthy` → `Process completed with exit code 1`, before Playwright runs.
- **Timeline attribution (correlation):** the Aug-10 nightly *included* #623 (postcode search) and PASSED — #623 is exonerated. The first failing night (Aug 11) was the **first to include Phase 28 (#630, `bb2ae65d`, merged Aug 10 11:38 BST)**. Prime suspect: a Phase-28 dev/prod-boundary change to compose/env/healthcheck that per-PR CI (which builds no compose stack) cannot catch.
- **No alerting exists:** `rg -uu workflow_run .github/workflows/` → none; `rg -uu -i nightly infra/monitoring/prometheus/alerts.yml` → none; `e2e-nightly.yml`'s only `if: failure()` step dumps logs *into* the failed run, visible only to someone already looking.

## Recommended actions

1. **Diagnose the Phase-28 change** that makes core-java unhealthy under the nightly's compose bring-up (compare against the Aug-10 green run). Likely a `.env`/healthcheck/role-provisioning change.
2. **Add a missed/failed-nightly alarm** — a `workflow_run` watcher or a scheduled check — so a dead full-stack lane escalates instead of sitting silent.
3. Once green, re-earn the `check-e2e-skip-budget` digest.

body:
## Summary

The `jtoye_backup` least-privilege dump role cannot read the newest table in the
`public` schema, so a `pg_dump` run as that role does not capture what it claims to.

## Impact

`infra/backups/create-backup-role.sql` grants the backup role SELECT on existing
tables/sequences and then, for future objects, runs `ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES ...
GRANT SELECT` **without a `FOR ROLE` clause**. When `FOR ROLE` is omitted the
defaults register against the *current* role — the postgres superuser running the
bootstrap — while Flyway creates every table as the migrator role. A
superuser-registered default therefore covers nothing the migrator makes, so any
table added by a migration after the backup script last ran inherits no privilege.

Measured on the live dev database (2026-08-10):

- readable tables: **40 of 41** (denominator: 41 regular relations in `public`)
- the one unreadable table is the newest, added by the most recent migration
- `SET ROLE jtoye_backup; COPY <that table> TO STDOUT;` — the exact per-table
  operation `pg_dump` performs — aborts with `permission denied for table ...`,
  exit code 1

## Failure direction (verified, not assumed)

`pg_dump` does **not** silently skip an unreadable table. It aborts the whole dump
on the first `permission denied`, so the failure is loud rather than silent — but
it means a scheduled backup as this role fails entirely once the gap exists, and a
backup that never completes is worse than one that skips a table. The read was
reproduced with `SET ROLE`, which faithfully mirrors what `pg_dump` issues.

## Fix

Add `FOR ROLE <migrator>` to both `ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES` statements so future
tables the migrator creates inherit SELECT, and re-run the existing
`GRANT SELECT ON ALL TABLES/SEQUENCES` lines so an existing database is brought
current (default privileges are not retroactive — they do not cover a table that
already exists). Both halves ship together.

## Acceptance

After running the repaired bootstrap against a database:

- `has_table_privilege('<backup role>', '<newest table>', 'SELECT')` is TRUE
- the count of backup-readable regular relations in `public` equals the total
  count of such relations (a relation with a denominator, not a bare count)
- a new table created by the migrator afterward is readable by the backup role
  with no further grant

## Notes

Repaired in the same change that introduces the non-owner runtime role
(SEC-04 / #552), which had the identical `ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES` shape and would
have reproduced the defect for the application role on the first table a future
migration adds. Sanitized: this is a privilege-grant defect; no credential value,
connection chain, or payload is involved.
title: jtoye_backup default privileges miss the newest table (ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES without FOR ROLE)

Follow-up from the pentest triage (SEC-02 / finding E1). Parent context: #551, record in
`docs/security/PENTEST-TRIAGE.md` §5.4.

**Impact.** The dev realm export no longer ships the unused public OAuth client that finding E1
pointed at — it was removed as part of the E1 audit, because a public client can be issued a token
with no client secret, and only the absence of an audience mapper keeps that token from being
accepted by the core API.

That removal is defeated by a second provisioning surface. A legacy operator script under
`infra/keycloak/` creates or updates the same client directly through the admin API, so anyone who
runs it by hand puts the client back into a realm the export says should not have it. The script is
not part of the automated bootstrap — neither the compose stack nor the development start-up script
invokes it — so this is a latent inconsistency rather than a live exposure, and it is filed rather
than fixed because the plan that removed the client had to keep its realm edit to a single clean
payload for the import that follows it.

Two architecture documents also still carry a token-request recipe naming the removed client. Those
recipes were already dead — the client's tokens authorise nowhere — and one of the same documents
already states, in a different section, that the client does not exist. So the documentation is
currently self-contradicting in both directions.

**Fix.**

- Remove the client's creation and update block from the legacy operator script, so the script and the
  committed realm export describe the same realm.
- Update the two architecture documents to drop the dead recipe and keep only the working one.
- Consider whether the operator script should exist at all now that the realm export is the
  provisioning path; if it stays, it needs a stated relationship to the export rather than an
  independent opinion about the realm.

**Acceptance.**

- Running the operator script against a realm imported from the current export leaves the client
  count unchanged — measured before and after, not asserted.
- A search of the tree for the client name returns only historical planning records, with a positive
  control proving the same search can still find a name that IS present. An empty search result is
  otherwise evidence about the pattern rather than about the tree.
- The two architecture documents no longer disagree with each other about whether the client exists.

**Not in scope.** The realm import itself, which a separate plan performs as one event carrying both
this phase's realm payloads.
title: A legacy Keycloak operator script recreates the unused public client the realm export no longer ships
